sentences.text:
Satyam Kori vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 December,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:62540
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Devnarayan Mishra
 On The 2 nd Of December, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 53141 of 2025

Satyam Kori
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Azad Krishna Bais - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri S.M. Patel - Panel Lawyer for the State.

Order 
This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023/ 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.290/2025 registered at Police Station - Gopalganj, District - Sagar (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) and 313 of IPC and Sections 3/4, 5l/6, 5(i)(ii)/6 of the POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 10.06.2025.

Applicant's first bail application i.e.
M.Cr.C. No.30583/2025 was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 20.08.2025.
2.

Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the statement of victim and her parents have been recorded and they have stated that the victim was major at the time of offence and as per the FIR itself, it is clear that the victim was the consenting party and they were in a love affair and they were talking with each other on mobile phone and the FIR was lodged NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:62540 2 MCRC-53141-2025 against the applicant, due to social pressure only as she got the pregnancy.
The applicant is a youth of 20 years.
Statement of the material witnesses have been recorded, therefore, no chance to influence the prosecution witnesses.
Trial will take time to be concluded, hence, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

3. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and has submitted that the victim was minor and her consent has no value, therefore, no case of bail is made out, hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
4. Heard the parties and perused the case diary.

sentences.text:
Looking to the age of both the parties at the time of offence and the statement of victim and her parents have been recorded, there is no apprehension to threatening the prosecution witnesses,
coupled with the fact that trial will take time to be concluded, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.
7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
8. Accordingly, Misc. Criminal Case stands disposed of.
